record.original_question: For the Gray-encoding permutation A006068 obtained by ordering nonnegative integers so that their binary-derivative strings are in lexicographic order, explain rigorously why the associated 4-regular graphs have the striking structure shown in the paper.

evidence.quote: Having introduced this notion, we can now define A006068 as the permutation of the integers in such an order that their derivatives are lexicographically ordered.
Most of these observations will be purely empirical – thus, we effectively list a large number of open problems: prove that said sequence indeed exhibits the observed type of structure.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a nonnegative integer $n$ with binary expansion $n = \sum_{i\ge 0} b_i 2^i$ (with $b_i \in \{0,1\}$ and only finitely many nonzero), define its binary derivative to be the infinite string $d(n) = (c_0, c_1, c_2, \ldots)$ where $c_i = b_i \oplus b_{i+1}$ (XOR). Order the nonnegative integers $n_0, n_1, n_2, \ldots$ so that the sequence of strings $d(n_0), d(n_1), d(n_2), \ldots$ is in lexicographic order; the resulting permutation $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $a(k) = n_k$, agrees with the OEIS sequence A006068 (the inverse Gray code).

Now form the following family of 4-regular graphs $G_N$ for each integer $N \ge 5$: take vertex set $V_N = \{0, 1, \ldots, N-1\}$ and, for each index $k$, connect $k$ to its two nearest neighbors on each side in the sequence $a$, i.e. join $k$ to $k\pm 1$ and $k\pm 2$ modulo $N$ in the ordering induced by $a$ (equivalently, take the 4-regular circulant-like graph defined by the consecutive 4-window structure of the sequence $(a(0), a(1), \ldots, a(N-1))$ when this list is reinterpreted as vertices via $a$).

Prove rigorously that the graphs $G_N$ exhibit the highly structured (non-random) macroscopic geometric pattern empirically observed when they are drawn with a force-directed (spring) layout: namely, identify and prove the precise combinatorial / geometric structure (e.g., number and shape of large-scale "lobes" or self-similar nested clusters, automorphism group, and growth rate of graph-theoretic diameter and bandwidth) of $G_N$ as $N \to \infty$.
artifact.category_tag: Gray code graphs from integer sequences
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a problem list paper that explicitly states the observations are empirical and asks for proofs of the observed structures. No subsequent work appears to have rigorously characterized the structure of the 4-regular graphs associated with A006068; the related survey on combinatorial Gray codes does not address this specific structural question.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorial Gray codes - an updated survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of combinatorial Gray codes and their generalizations.
status_evidence.claim: A recent survey on Gray codes does not record a resolution of the structural problem for the A006068-graphs.
